word.title: Property Has One Parent
word.description: Every property node that hangs under anything hangs, by IS_A_PROPERTY_OF, under exactly one node.

graphRule.name: property-has-one-parent
graphRule.says: every property node that hangs under anything hangs, by `IS_A_PROPERTY_OF`, under exactly one node. A concept's primary property (the node with `IS_THE_PRIMARY_PROPERTY_FOR` to its header) hangs under its own concept's JSON schema node; every other property hangs under a property: its concept's primary property at the top level, or its parent property when nested (BIBLE §6). A property under no parent isn't judged, since `POST /api/normalize/generate-property-tree` unhooks the properties a new schema drops on purpose. A property node with two parents leaves its concept's tree tangled, and the property writes refuse such a concept (`tangled-tree`, ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0018).
graphRule.kind: a graph rule, about every property node, whoever made it.
graphRule.refusesOrReports: it only reports. No write the operations make can break it, and the property writes already refuse a tangled tree.
graphRule.check: `rules check` runs it over the whole graph, one concept (its primary property, its property tree, and what hangs directly on its JSON schema node) or one node: the rule's `scan` lists every property node with a parent in the scope, and its `violations` judges them. Each of its reads runs over every item at once: three judge each node's shape, one more reads what the primary properties hang under, and the rest, which find each finding's concepts and what its parents are, run only for the findings. Each finding has a code: `more-than-one-parent`, `parent-not-a-property` or `primary-property-misplaced`. It names the node, the concepts whose trees hold it, and each parent with what it is (a primary property, a property, a JSON schema node or another kind of node) and whether it belongs to the node's own concept. A finding has an id, which changes when the node's parents do. Today's `POST /api/normalize/enumerate` broke it before story graph-operations-first-slice #45, by hanging a property on its target concept's schema, and so did `POST /api/normalize/create-property`, by hanging a top-level property on the schema and giving one name under two parents one node.
graphRule.repair: `rules repair` takes off a property's `IS_A_PROPERTY_OF` to its own concept's JSON schema node when the property also hangs under one parent in that concept's tree, keeping that link, in one recorded write that signs nothing. It changes the instance's own concepts, and a firmware concept only with `firmwareOverride: true`. Every other finding is left as a choice, with why and the way on: a concept that isn't the instance's own is its author's claim (D4); a node two concepts' trees share, or one under two properties of a tree, has no operation to take one link out yet; a property hung only on a schema node gets a node in its tree from `graph add-property` or `graph set-schema`; a misplaced primary property has `POST /api/normalize/skeleton`. The repair names the relationship elements that still record a link it took off, which `graph delete-node` deletes.
graphRule.enforcedBy: a check: `rules check`, with `rules repair`. The rule's code is in `src/operations/rules/property-has-one-parent.js`; the operations are `src/operations/catalog/rules/check.js` and `src/operations/catalog/rules/repair.js`, with what they share in `src/operations/catalog/rules/_rules.js`. Built in story graph-operations-first-slice #45 (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0045).

code.summary: Every property node that hangs under anything hangs under exactly one node: a primary property under its own concept's JSON schema node, every other property under a property.
